Just head over to Steam and download GTFO during the free weekend period (13-16 of June)

notes.title: The GTFO Streamathon speedrun contest
notes.content:
We recently announced our big [b]GTFO Streamathon[/b] charity event in June where we aim to complete all [b]83 expeditions[/b] in the game during a [b]96 hour long livestream[/b]. And as you can imagine, we are going to need some help with that. Developers being bad at their game and all of that. 

We want to invite the best speedrunning team to our office in Stockholm, Sweden to help us with this enormous task. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31404391/6f4ede179bc23fbbe799ab19658a16a3a5978d1a.png[/img]

We will only count the submissions to Speedrun.com/GTFO during the competition period which starts now, the 30th of April, and ends the 8th of May, 23:59 CEST. It doesn’t need to be verified during this period though. Full [url=https://gtfo.gl/toc_speedrun]Terms and Conditions here[/url].

[h3]FAQ[/h3]
[b]I want to compete in several teams, is that ok?[/b]
Yes, but you can of course only win with one of them

[b]How do I submit a run to Speedrun.com?[/b]
Check out Speedrun.com/GTFO for information (account required).

[b]Do previous records count?[/b]
As stated above, no. Only fresh runs.

[b]What costs are covered if I win?[/b]
Travel and hotel costs are covered, other expenses are on you. Full Terms and Conditions [url=https://gtfo.gl/toc_speedrun]here[/url].

More questions? Reach out to the Community Manager on the official Discord server or email community@gtfothegame.com.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31404391/74c9558ca01257195470caad3f961be29a24c0d3.png[/img]

notes.title: Nominate GTFO as The Best Game You Suck At
notes.content:
[h3][b]GTFO is The Best Game You Suck(ed) At[/b][/h3]
We were browsing through the different categories for [b]The Steam Awards[/b], and we found (among others) two very fitting for GTFO: [b]Better With Friends[/b], and [b]The Best Game You Suck At[/b]. 

Then we looked at the descriptions of each of them:
[b]"Better With Friends"[/b] - [i]There are some games out there that just aren't the same when you play by yourself. Maybe you need to have a friend to watch your back. Maybe you need to have a friend that you can stab in their back. Either way, mirth is awaiting those who gather friends to play these games.[/i]

[b]"Best Game You Suck At"[/b] - [i]This is the game that rewards persistence, and is not for the faint of heart. It's the toughest game we've ever loved.[/i]

Okay, we all know that GTFO is indeed Better With Friends - we’d even say [i]it’s impossible without friends [/i](well, if your name isn’t RandomKenny) - and [b]with the recently added match-making function[/b], you can hopefully make new friends, too. 

But the description for [b]Best Game You Suck At seems like it was written for GTFO[/b], right? If you don’t agree with us, [b]you’re free to choose any category you deem fit[/b]. We will love you anyway. Thanks for your support! <3

[h3][b]We’re 20% off, tell your friends![/b][/h3]
GTFO will be a part of The Steam Autumn Sale, starting about… now. So, if you know any friends that can handle The Complex, let them know. [b]Tip:[/b] GTFO is the perfect (early) Christmas gift, during these quarantine times. 

[h3][b]GTFO turns 1 year old on December 9th[/b][/h3]
Our Early Access baby is growing. Four Rundowns later, and she’s already 1 year old. [b]To celebrate, we’re cooking some stuff[/b] for our beloved community. 

[b]Stay tuned, keep distance, and clean your hands regularly[/b].

notes.title: GTFO got new enemies and missions with today's Infection update
notes.content:
GTFO’s big free Infection update is out today, bringing new maps, weapons, enemies and objectives to the tense tactical survival-horror shooter. It’s brought a whole new Rundown with it too, wiping away the old one to make room for a bunch of new levels.

If you’ve not had the chance to play GTFO yet, it’s a super tense co-op experience where you and four friends play as prisoners dropped into a mysterious underground complex. You have to be pretty stealthy and extremely coordinated to get to your objectives, because there are some very angry zombie-things that demolish you in hordes if you don’t.

notes.title: GTFO: The Road Ahead
notes.content:
[h1]Entering the Test Stage[/h1]
[b]We’ll soon be entering GTFO’s test stage.[/b] How long this stage will be depends on how quickly we can implement the features, squash the bugs and nail the balancing. We’re testing because the game genuinely needs it.

We’re going to be depending on you - our community - to help GTFO reach its full potential. In other words, this won’t be beta test that’s actually a game demo released close to the final game launch. [b]We have a lot work left on GTFO before the game is completed, which allow this to be a proper test - one that benefits and influences the game’s development in a major way.[/b]


[h1]No Final Release This Spring[/h1]
“But I thought the game was close to finished” you may say. And yes, we have said that [b]GTFO would come out in the spring of 2019 - but, as is often the case in this beautiful mayhem that is game development; things have proven more difficult and time-consuming than we first anticipated.[/b]

GTFO is designed to be continuously expanded upon post release, meaning that almost no element in the game can be designed or coded as a one-off feature. Instead, everything must be part of flexible, scalable, overarching systems. These systems are tough to both develop and to test.

[b]Even though our team has about a century worth of combined experience, none of us have made a game that looks quite like this on the inside.[/b] It’s a huge technical challenge to realize with such a small team - and we know that in order to avoid a world of problems later on, we must lay an incredibly solid foundation now.

We acknowledge and fully understand anyone who is disappointed in the fact that GTFO isn’t coming out as a finished, fully-fledged game this spring. We hate to let our community down like this but we can’t release the game when it’s simply not done. [b]In the fall of 2018 we prematurely predicted when the game was going to be ready - and we apologize for that.[/b]

Despite the false step on our end, we hope you’re excited for the next stage in the development of GTFO; when the community is invited to test the game. There’s no better way to develop a game focused on cooperation than in cooperation with its community!


[h1]Proper Testing - What It Means[/h1]
[b]The fact that this is a genuine test stage means that the tests will not always be as enjoyable as you wish they would be:[/b] If we’re testing the network code, expect there to be network issues (if the code was verified to work 100%, we wouldn’t have to test it.)

We ask you to calibrate your expectations accordingly: During tests, you’re not going to be playing a fully polished and feature complete game. [b]You must have patience and remember the purpose of the tests.[/b]

As we see it, you’re doing us a favor by helping us test the game - that’s something we are grateful for and also why we won’t use the tests as a marketing ploy or a pre-order bonus.

[h1]The Roadmap[/h1]
As part of our effort to be more transparent, [b]we will maintain a public roadmap that indicates what types of features will be worked on and tested during the test stage.[/b]

This roadmap does not contain any dates because we can’t be sure how much time it will take to test each and every element. We’re a small team and GTFO is a very ambitious project - planning is a real challenge. From now on, we won’t go public with dates until we know we can hit them.

The purpose of the roadmap is to make you aware of what you have to look forward to, but you have to keep in mind that things will change and [b]the roadmap cannot be seen as a contract or a promise of any kind[/b]. The order of things will shift and features will be added or removed based on the data and feedback we collect throughout the tests phases.

[url=http://gtfothegame.com/roadmap/]You can find the roadmap publicly on the GTFO homepage[/url].

[h1]Early Access[/h1]
[b]The ultimate purpose of the test stage is to make GTFO enough feature complete and stable to go into Early Access.[/b] Through Early Access, GTFO’s development can continue to be community-driven while also allowing us to bring in some money and reduce the financial risk that this project entails. As you may or may not know, we have - up until this point - been developing GTFO  without any external funding, in order to enjoy complete creative freedom.

[b]We are well aware that Early Access as a concept has some negative connotations[/b], with some games being stuck in what seems like perpetual Early Access and the developers seeing it as an excuse to never bring the game to a finalized, polished state.

[b]We will commit to doing an Early Access stage the way it’s supposed to be done: With transparency, developer-community dialog and clear goals[/b] - goals that will bring GTFO out of Early Access as soon as they’re achieved. We hope the test stage that precedes the Early Access stage will prove that we’re serious about doing things the right way.

[b]Thank you for your support,[/b]
10 Chambers Collective

notes.title: PC Gamer: "You need teamwork, stealth, and steady nerves to survive co-op horror FPS GTFO"
notes.content:
Christopher Livingston of PC Gamer stopped by our booth at E3 to play GTFO - for the first time playable at E3. Here's some of the stuff he had to say about the game, and 7 minutes (!) of previously unseen gameplay of GTFO. [b][url=https://www.pcgamer.com/you-need-teamwork-stealth-and-steady-nerves-to-survive-co-op-horror-fps-gtfo/]Find the article in full here[/url][/b].

[i]"The depths of GTFO are to be approached slowly and cautiously, with careful coordination between your team members. It's not a game for bursting boldly into unexplored chambers spraying bullets wildly: there simply aren't enough bullets for that. Ammo is scarce even from the start, and each area should be carefully combed for every last ammo pack and medkit, and then shared among the team depending on who needs it most."[/i]

https://youtu.be/c29boXcbGbo
[i]"I had a great time with the level of GTFO I played: it's a tense and creepy horror shooter that blends long periods of tense exploration and stealth with sudden freak-out bursts of chaotic gunplay when that stealth doesn't go quite right."[/i]

[h1]Interview with Ulf Andersson[/h1]
Right after landing in Los Angeles, Ulf Andersson, founder of 10 Chambers Collective and Creative Director of GTFO, visited Geoff Keighley at YouTube Live @ E3 to talk about GTFO and show some new gameplay. You can find the interview and gameplay footage here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=798IMM0LQ7c

Stay tuned for even more news about GTFO during E3.
